(B)

solution: (A) every는 뒤에 단수명사가 오고, ‘every+시간 단수 명사’는 ‘매 ~마다’라는 뜻을 나타내므로, every와 함께 ‘주말마다’를 뜻 하는 단수명사 weekend가 적절하다. (B) 감각동사 feel은 보어로 형용사가 와야 하므로 부사 so의 수식을 받아 형용사구를 이루는 형용사 happy가 적절하다. (C) be의 보어 자리에서 명사구 a great chance를 수식하여 명 사구를 이루어야 하며, to부정사가 ‘~할’이라는 뜻으로 앞의 명 사구를 수식할 수 있으므로, to부정사인 to share가 적절하다.

body:
People say, “Every dog has its day.” In Nepal, this
saying is literally true. Dogs have been an important
part of Nepalese culture for hundreds of years. The
Nepalese believe that dogs are helpers of the god
of death and guide souls to heaven. Because of
this belief, Nepal has a special day to celebrate
dogs. This dog festival usually takes place in
October or November. On this day, people give
dogs flower necklaces and delicious food. They also
put a red mark on dogs’ foreheads to wish them
good luck. They even bow to dogs to show them
love and thanks.

Some animals have been our friends for thousands
of years. They have helped and protected us. To
celebrate these animal friends, people in Ireland and
Nepal hold special festivals every year. These
festivals show a strong bond between humans and
animals.
Wild Goat Festival in Ireland
Every year from August 10 to 12, people in
Killorglin hold a festival to celebrate wild goats.
There is one story about the festival’s beginning.
When the English army was attacking Ireland in the
17th century, they came across a group of wild
goats in a field. Most of the goats ran away to the
mountains, but one goat ran toward the village.
When the villagers saw the tired and scared goat,
they realized that (A)__________________________. Thanks
to the goat, the villagers were able to prepare and
protect themselves.
Since then, people in Killorglin have celebrated
wild goats with this festival. At the festival, people
crown a goat to show thanks to it. They also give
it a lot of food and take good care of it. People
then parade, dance, and sing.
Dog Festival in Nepal
People say, “Every dog has its day.” In Nepal, this
saying is literally true. Dogs have been an important
part of Nepalese culture for hundreds of years. The
Nepalese believe that dogs are helpers of the god
of death and guide souls to heaven. Because of
this belief, Nepal has a special day to celebrate
dogs. This dog festival usually takes place in
October or November. On this day, people give
dogs flower necklaces and delicious food. They also
put a red mark on dogs’ foreheads to wish them
good luck. They even bow to dogs to show them
love and thanks.

solution: 건물을 청소하는 데 사용하던 강한 세제 때문에 건물이 손상되었고, 그 세제는 새의 배설물을 닦기 위해 사용했으며, 새들은 거미를 먹기 위해 건물에 왔다고 했으므로 빈칸에는 ❸ ‘배설물을 남긴 새들을 불러들였다’가 적절하다.

body:
When we have a problem, we often wonder what the solution is. We ⓐcan sometimes find one by repeating the question, “Why?” The following story shows the importance of asking “why” questions.
The Jefferson Memorial is a famous building in Washington D.C. It was built to honor Thomas Jefferson, the third president of the U.S. One day, building caretakers noticed a lot of damage to the building. They asked themselves a question, “Why is this building so damaged?” They soon realized that they were using strong soap to clean the building.
Then, they asked another question, “Why do we need to use strong soap?” From this question, they realized that they used it ⓑcleaning bird droppings off the building. They kept asking, “Why do birds like to come to this building?” The answer was that they came to the building to eat spiders. This led to another ⓒinteresting question, “Why do spiders like to come to this building, then?” They realized that spiders came to the building to eat bugs.
Then, they asked again, “Why do so many bugs come to this building?” Since they could not find the answer, they asked a bug expert for help. He explained why ⓓcame many bugs to the building. He said, “Bugs are most active at sunset. Since you turn on the lights at sunset, bugs are drawn to the lights.” This was an important finding in solving the problem.
The solution was very simple. They turned on the lights only after it was completely dark. This stopped bugs from coming. With fewer bugs, there ⓔwere also fewer spiders, birds, and droppings. Since they didn’t have to use strong soap, the building was no longer ⓕdamaging by their cleaning.

윗글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: The Answer Behind All the Answers
One Good Question Is All You Need
Fix the Problem First, Ask Questions Later
Small Animals, Big Trouble at a Famous Building

solution:

body:
ⓐ Please tell me how was your trip to Busan.
ⓑ I can’t remember who gave me this key ring.
ⓒ I wonder why did she leave the party so early.
ⓓ He won the singing contest since he practiced every day.
ⓔ Since my little sister to be sick, my mom stayed home with her.
다음 중 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
solution:
어법상 어색한 것의 개수는 3개이다.
ⓐ how was your trip to Busan → how your trip to Busan was (동사 tell은 ‘tell+간접목적어+직접목적어’ 어순의 4형식으로 쓰이며, 직접목적어 자리에 간접의문문이 왔으므로 ‘의문사+주어+동사’ 어순이 되어야 한다. 따라서 의문사 how 뒤의 was your trip to Busan을 ‘주어+동사’의 어순이 되도록 your trip to Busan was로 고쳐야 한다.)
ⓒ why did she leave → why she left (동사 wonder의 목적어로 의문사가 있는 의문문이 간접의문문으로 쓰였으므로 ‘의문사+주어+동사’ 어순이 되어야 한다. 따라서 의문문을 만들기 위해 쓰인 과거 시제 조동사 did를 삭제하고, 동사 leave를 과거형 left로 바꾸어 why she left로 고쳐야 한다.)
ⓔ to be → was (‘~하기 때문에’라는 의미로 이유를 나타내는 접속사 Since 뒤에는 ‘주어+동사’를 갖춘 완전한 절이 와야 한다. 주어 my little sister 뒤에 동사가 아닌 to부정사 to be가 쓰였으므로, 과거의 일을 나타내며 3인칭 단수 주어에 수일치한 과거형 be동사 was로 고쳐야 한다.)
오답
ⓑ 동사 remember의 목적어로 의문사 who로 시작하는 간접의문문이 쓰였으며, 의문사 who가 의문사이자 주어 역할을 하므로 ‘의문사+동사 ~’ 어순으로 쓴 who gave 이하는 적절하다.
ⓓ ‘~하기 때문에’라는 의미의 이유를 나타내는 접속사 since 뒤에 ‘주어+동사 ~’의 완전한 절(he ~ day)이 이어진 것은 적절하며, since절이 주절의 역할을 하는 완전한 절 뒤에 이어질 때 콤마 없이 쓰는 것도 알맞다.

body:
ⓐI am running to catch the bus since got up late. ⓑSince the bus is already at the bus stop, I need to hurry. ⓒI wonder when does the bus leave. ⓓI don’t know how much time I have before the bus leaves.
다음 그림에 대한 설명으로 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
solution:
ⓐ since got up late → since I got up late (흐름상 ‘나는 늦게 일어났기 때문에’라는 이유를 나타내야 하므로 ‘~하기 때문에’라는 의미의 접속사 since 뒤에 ‘주어+동사’를 갖춘 완전한 절이 와야 한다. since 뒤에 주어가 빠져 있으므로 주어 I를 쓴 since I got up late로 고쳐야 한다.)
ⓒ when does the bus leave → when the bus leaves (의문사가 있는 의문문이 동사 wonder의 목적어로 쓰인 간접의문문이므로 ‘의문사+주어+동사’의 어순이 되어야 한다. 따라서 의문문을 만들기 위해 쓰인 조동사 does를 삭제하고, 주어 the bus가 3인칭 단수이므로 이에 수일치하여 leave를 단수동사 leaves로 바꾸어 when the bus leaves로 고쳐야 한다.)
오답
ⓑ Since는 ‘~하기 때문에’라는 의미의 이유를 나타내는 접속사로 쓰여 뒤에 ‘주어+동사’ 형태의 완전한 절(the bus ~ stop)이 왔으며, 버스가 이미 정류장에 와 있다는 이유와 나는 서둘러야 한다는 결과를 연결하고 있으므로 적절하다.
ⓓ 동사 know의 목적어로 쓰인 간접의문문이 ‘의문사구(how much time)+주어(I)+동사(have)’의 어순으로 쓰였으므로 적절하다. 또한 접속사 before가 이끄는 시간의 부사절에서는 미래의 일을 현재 시제로 나타내므로, 3인칭 단수 주어 the bus에 수일치시킨 현재형 동사 leaves를 쓴 것도 적절하다.
제시문 ⓐ나는 늦게 일어났기 때문에 버스를 타기 위해 달리고 있다. ⓑ버스가 이미 정류장에 와 있기 때문에, 나는 서둘러야 한다. ⓒ나는 버스가 언제 출발하는지 궁금하다. ⓓ나는 버스가 출발하기 전에 내게 시간이 얼마나 있는지 모른다.

body: 다음 중 짝지어진 대화가 어색한 것은?
choices:
A: I don’t think I can pass the test.
B: Don’t worry. I’m sure you can do it.

A: You look worried. What’s wrong?
B: I’m worried about my grandfather. He’s in the hospital.

A: I bought a cute doll for Mina’s birthday. Will she like it?
B: I’m certain she will. She loves cute dolls.

A: I’m worried about my cat. He has been sick for days.
B: That’s terrific! Did you take him to the vet?

A: I’m concerned about the group project.
B: You’ve worked hard on it. I’m sure it will work out well.
solution:
A가 며칠째 아픈 고양이가 걱정된다고 말하고 있으므로 그것을 훌륭하다고 표현하는 것은 알맞지 않다. ‘That’s terrific!‘을 ’That’s too bad.‘ 등의 유감을 나타내는 표현으로 고쳐야 한다.
A: 나는 내 고양이가 걱정돼. 그가 며칠째 아파.
B: 훌륭해!(→그것 참 안 됐다.) 그를 수의사에게 데려갔니?
오답
① A: 나는 시험에 통과할 수 없을 것 같아.
B: 걱정하지 마. 분명 네가 해낼 수 있다고 확신해.
② A: 너 걱정이 있어 보여. 무슨 일이니?
B: 나는 할아버지가 걱정돼. 그는 병원에 계셔.
③ A: 나는 미나의 생일을 위해 귀여운 인형을 샀어. 그녀가 그것을 좋아할까?
B: 그녀가 분명히 좋아할 거라고 확신해. 그녀는 귀여운 인형을 아주 좋아해.
⑤ A: 나는 조별 과제가 걱정돼.
B: 너는 그 과제를 열심히 해 왔잖아. 분명 잘 될 것이라고 확신해.

body:
G: ______ He plays video games all night.
B: Oh, no. Is he getting enough sleep?
G: No, he’s always tired during the day.
B: You should talk to your mom. I’m sure he will listen to her.
G: Yes, I think I should.
다음 대화의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: I’m proud of my little brother John.
I’m thankful to my little brother John.

solution:
빈칸 뒤에서 소녀가 남동생이 밤새도록 비디오 게임을 한다고 말하고, 소년이 그가 잠을 충분히 자는지 염려하며 엄마에게 이야기해 보라고 조언하고 있으므로 빈칸에는 남동생에 대한 걱정을 표현하는 ③ ‘나는 내 남동생 John이 걱정돼.’가 적절하다.
오답
① 나는 내 남동생 John이 자랑스러워.

⑤ 나는 내 남동생 John에게 사과할 필요가 있어.

body:
G: I’m worried about my presentation next week.
B: You have worked on it for weeks. Why are you so worried?
G: I don’t want to make a mistake in front of others.
B: Then, why don’t you practice in front of your family? I’m sure it will be helpful.
G: Okay, I will try. Thanks.
다음 대화의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: a good place to practice for a presentation
the girl’s hard work on her presentation for weeks
the boy’s own experience of giving a presentation
the family’s help with choosing a presentation topic

When we have a problem, we often wonder ⓐwhat the solution is. We can sometimes find ⓑone by repeating the question, “Why?” The following story shows the importance of ⓒasking “why” questions.
The Jefferson Memorial is a famous building in Washington D.C. It was built ⓓto honor Thomas Jefferson, the third president of the U.S. One day, building caretakers noticed a lot of damage to the building. They asked themselves a question, “Why is this building so damaged?” They soon (A)realized that they were ⓔused strong soap to clean the building.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓔ used → using (주어 they는 building caretakers를 가리키며 그들은 강한 세제를 ‘사용하는’ 주체이고 뒤에 목적어 strong soap이 이어지므로, 수동태가 아니라 능동태가 되어야 하며, 앞의 be동사 were에 이어져 과거의 특정 시점에 강한 세제를 계속 사용하고 있던 중인 것을 나타내는 과거진행형(be+-ing)이 되도록 과거분사 used를 현재분사 using으로 고쳐야 한다.)
오답
ⓐ 동사 wonder의 목적어 자리에 ‘의문사+주어+동사’ 어순의 간접의문문이 쓰였고, 뒤에 be동사 is의 보어가 빠진 불완전한 절(the solution is)이 이어지므로, 의문사이자 is의 보어 역할을 함께 하는 의문대명사 what은 적절하다.
ⓑ 앞 문장의 solution과 같은 종류의 불특정한 하나, 즉 a solution을 대신하는 부정대명사 one은 적절하다. 참고로, it은 앞에 나온 바로 그 특정한 대상을 가리킬 때 쓴다.
ⓒ 전치사 of의 목적어 자리이자, 명사구 “why” questions를 취할 수 있는 동명사 asking은 적절하다.
ⓓ 앞의 명사구 The Jefferson Memorial을 가리키는 주어 It으로 시작하는 완전한 절 It was built에 이어지고 있으므로, ‘~하기 위해’의 의미를 가지므로 ‘목적’을 나타내는 부사적 용법의 to부정사구 to honor은 적절하다.

body:
Then, they asked another question, “Why do we need to use strong soap?”
(A) They kept asking, “Why do birds like to come to this building?” The answer was that they came to the building to eat spiders.
(B) This led to another interesting question, “Why do spiders like to come to this building, then?” They realized that spiders came to the building to eat bugs.
(C) From this question, they realized that they used it to clean bird droppings off the building.
다음 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 주어진 문장의 강한 세제를 왜 사용해야 하는지에 대한 질문을 this question으로 받고, strong soap을 it으로 가리켜 그들이 새의 배설물을 닦기 위해 그것을 사용한다는 것을 깨달았다는 내용의 (C)로 이어지고, (C)의 마지막에 언급된 bird droppings와 관련하여 새가 이 건물에 오는 것을 좋아하는 이유에 대한 질문에, 새들이 거미를 먹으러 온다는 답을 얻었다는 내용의 (A)로 이어지며, (A)의 마지막에 언급된 새가 거미를 먹으러 온다는 답을 This로 받아 그것이 거미가 왜 이 건물에 오는지에 대한 또 다른 흥미로운 질문으로 이어져 거미가 벌레를 먹으러 온다는 것을 깨달았다는 내용의 (B)로 이어지는 것이 적절하다.

body:
Then, they asked again, “Why do so many bugs come to this building?” Since they could not find the answer, they asked a bug expert for help. He explained why many bugs came to the building. He said, “Bugs are most active at sunset. Since you turn on the lights at sunset, bugs are drawn to the lights.” This was an important finding in solving the problem.
The solution was very simple. They turned on the lights only after it was completely dark. This stopped bugs from coming. With fewer bugs, there were also fewer spiders, birds, and droppings. Since they didn’t have to use strong soap, the building was no longer damaged by their cleaning.
(they = building caretakers)
다음 글을 아래와 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?

solution:
(A) 곤충 전문가가 해 질 무렵에 불을 켜기 때문에 벌레들이 불빛에 이끌린다고 설명했고, 벌레가 줄어들자 거미, 새, 배설물도 함께 줄어 더 이상 강한 세제를 사용할 필요가 없어졌으므로, 문제가 실제로 건물의 ‘불빛’에서 시작되었다는 뜻의 lights가 적절하다.
(B) 관리인들이 완전히 어두워진 후에만 불을 켜도록 바꾼 매우 간단한 해결책으로 건물의 손상을 멈추었다고 했으므로, ‘작은’ 변화로 충분했다는 뜻의 small이 적절하다.
요약문 전문가는 관리인들이 문제가 실제로 건물의 (A)불빛에서 시작되었다는 것을 알도록 도왔고, (B)작은 변화가 건물의 손상을 멈추기에 충분했다.

③ 세제 작은
④ 새 엄청난
⑤ 세제 엄청난

body:
When we have a problem, we often wonder what the solution is. We can sometimes find one by repeating the question, “Why?” The following story shows the importance of asking “why” questions.
The Jefferson Memorial is a famous building in Washington D.C. It was built to honor Thomas Jefferson, the third president of the U.S. One day, building caretakers noticed a lot of damage to the building. They asked ⓐthem a question, “Why is this building so damaged?” They soon realized that they were using strong soap to clean the building.
Then, they asked another question, “Why do we need ⓑto use strong soap?” From this question, they realized that they used it to clean bird droppings off the building. They kept asking, “Why do birds like to come to this building?” The answer was that they came to the building to eat spiders. This led to another interesting question, “Why do spiders like to come to this building, then?” They realized that spiders came to the building to eat bugs.
Then, they asked again, “Why do ⓒso much bugs come to this building?” Since they could not find the answer, they asked a bug expert for help. He explained why many bugs came to the building. He said, “Bugs are most active at sunset. Since you turn on the lights at sunset, bugs are drawn to the lights.” This was an important finding in ⓓsolve the problem.
The solution was very simple. They turned on the lights only (A)______. This stopped bugs from coming. With fewer bugs, there were also fewer spiders, birds, and droppings. Since they ⓔdidn’t have to use strong soap, the building was no longer damaged by their cleaning.
윗글을 읽고 다음 질문에 대한 알맞은 대답이 되도록 주어진 <조건>에 맞게 빈칸을 완성하시오.
Q. What was the real cause of the damage to the building?
<조건>
• of, powerful, time을 사용할 것
• 동명사구를 사용할 것
→ It was not the ______ ______, but the ______ ______ ______ ______ the lights.
answer: powerful soap, time of turning on
